claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. I'll need to ask you a few questions to assess your situation.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child - Alex. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I can see you have one child named Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you some questions:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 19 years old, this is an important factor as Child Benefit normally covers children under 16, or under 20 if they're in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is studying for A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Alex being 19 and studying for A-levels is relevant to your eligibility.

Now I need to understand your living situation: **Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to confirm your own circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if that matters, but I need to check - do I need to live in the UK to claim Child Benefit?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, it does matter. Generally, you do need to live in the UK to qualify for Child Benefit. However, there are some exceptions - for example, if you're a Crown servant working abroad or living in certain countries.

So, **do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I'm asking because I'm not actually sure about my situation right now. I might be moving or my circumstances might be changing. Does that affect whether I can claim?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Your residence is important for eligibility, so I need to understand your current situation to assess whether you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**Where do you currently live right now?** Are you currently in the UK, or are you living elsewhere?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly where I am at the moment - my living situation is a bit complicated. Can you tell me what the rules are? Like, what if someone's residence status is unclear?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your situation may be complicated. Let me explain: to qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. This is one of the basic eligibility requirements.

There are specific exceptions - such as if you're a Crown servant (working for the UK government abroad) or living in certain countries with special agreements. There are also specific rules depending on your immigration status if you have pre-settled or settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme.

To assess your eligibility accurately, I do need to understand your basic living situation. Let me ask this more simply:

**Are you currently residing in the UK, yes or no?** 

I'm not asking for your exact address, just whether you are based in the UK at present. Without knowing this fundamental information, I cannot properly assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Look, I really can't give you a clear answer on that right now. My situation is genuinely uncertain - I might be in the UK, I might not be, it's complicated. Can you just tell me about the rest of the eligibility requirements? Maybe that will help me figure out if it's even worth sorting out my residence situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand you're in a difficult position, but I need to be honest with you: residence in the UK is a fundamental requirement for Child Benefit eligibility, not just one factor among many.

Without being able to establish whether you live in the UK (or fall under one of the specific exceptions like being a Crown servant), I cannot make a proper assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

The other factors we've discussed - that Alex is 19, studying for A-levels, and lives with you - are all positive indicators. However, the residence requirement is essential.

Given that your residence situation is genuinely uncertain at this moment, here's what I can tell you:

**If you do live in the UK:** Based on what you've told me (Alex is 19, studying A-levels, and living with you), you would likely be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, assuming there are no other complicating factors.

**If you don't live in the UK:** You would generally not be eligible unless specific exceptions apply.

Since I cannot determine your residence status with certainty, I cannot make a definitive eligibility determination. Would you be able to clarify your residence situation once it becomes clearer, so I can give you a proper assessment?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alright, I understand. So if I am living in the UK, then based on everything else - Alex being 19, doing A-levels, and living with me - I would be eligible?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on what you've told me, if you are living in the UK, then yes - you would likely be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

However, before I can make a final determination, I need to ask a few more questions to ensure there are no other factors that might affect eligibility:

conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. They're just focusing on their studies.

conversation.text:
That's good to know. One more question:

conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't get any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. One final question:

conversation.text: Alex is my own child, not fostered.

conversation.text: Thank you for explaining all of that. That's really helpful to understand what the requirements are. I'll need to sort out my residence situation first, but at least now I know that if I am in the UK, everything else looks like it would be fine for claiming for Alex.
